pr_title: fix: make count_match docs and extract_all docs/impl consistent around zero matches

issue_context.title: str.count_match docs and str.extract_all implementation are inconsistent around non-matching strings
issue_context.body:
Suppose we have

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["123 bla 45 asd", "xyz 678 910t", "foo", None]})
```

The docs for `str.count_match` says

> Contains null values if the original value is null or the regex captures nothing.

However, it (correctly) returns zero if there were no matches:

```python
>>> df.select(pl.col("foo").str.count_match(r"\d"))
shape: (4, 1)
┌──────┐
│ foo  │
│ ---  │
│ u32  │
╞══════╡
│ 5    │
│ 6    │
│ 0    │
│ null │
└──────┘
```

 On the contrary, `str.extract_all` returns null when there were no matches, when I believe it should return the empty list. Currently we have:

```python
>>> df.select(pl.col("foo").str.extract_all(r"\d"))
shape: (4, 1)
┌───────────────────┐
│ foo               │
│ ---               │
│ list[str]         │
╞═══════════════════╡
│ ["1", "2", … "5"] │
│ ["6", "7", … "0"] │
│ null              │
│ null              │
└───────────────────┘
```

I believe it should be

```python
>>> df.select(pl.col("foo").str.extract_all(r"\d"))
shape: (4, 1)
┌───────────────────┐
│ foo               │
│ ---               │
│ list[str]         │
╞═══════════════════╡
│ ["1", "2", … "5"] │
│ ["6", "7", … "0"] │
│ []                │
│ null              │
└───────────────────┘
```
